    November 9, 2026 10:02 AM

    UPDATE Nov. 9, 2026

    Drought conditions persist in much of Northern Colorado. As a result, Broomfield will remain in a Drought Watch going into this winter season. Because winter snowpack is the main driver of water supply for Broomfield and most of Colorado, it will likely be unknown until early Spring if current drought conditions will improve or worsen in 2027. While communities in southwestern Colorado have experienced devastating floods in recent weeks, snowpack is off to a slow start so far in Northern Colorado. Under CCOB’s Drought Response Plan, Water Utilities staff will track snowpack and other conditions throughout the winter and will provide updates to the Broomfield Council and community as needed.

    What can residents do this winter to prepare for drought? Remember to winterize your lawn irrigation system before a hard freeze to avoid damaging the system. Your lawn will remain dormant throughout the Winter and does not generally need any irrigation until Spring. However, during prolonged dry periods in the winter, trees, shrubs and perennials may need irrigation. Water them by hand one to two times a month, but only when air temperatures exceed 40 degrees and there is no snow cover, which allows the water to soak deeply down to the roots without freezing.

    Visit Broomfield.org/DroughtStatus for all the details.
